title: Protocol with an Associated Type
hints: `associatedtype Item` lets each conforming type choose its element type.
Conform both types, then write a generic function whose `where` clause says the two item types match and are `Equatable`.
`where C1.Item == C2.Item, C1.Item: Equatable` and compare `a[i] == b[i]` for every index.
jsBridge: The Swift book's `Container` protocol: an associated `Item`, plus generic functions constrained on it. It's the foundation of how `Collection` works. TS would write `interface Container<Item>`, and Swift infers `Item` from the conformer's methods.

compass.q: In TS, `IntBag implements Container<number>` states the type. How does Swift infer `Item` from `append(_:)`?
What happens if inference is ambiguous? How do you state `typealias Item = Int` explicitly?
`func allMatch<C1: Container, C2: Container>(…) where C1.Item == C2.Item`: why do you need the `where`?
Would you design your own container protocol in app code, or just use `Collection`?
